problems: The blind guess (a small cartoon humanoid with an oval head, one leg and spiky hands) describes the blue figure at upper left, not the intended split oar. The guess is therefore wrong for the subject.
The blue humanoid figure is a stray element that does not belong to The Split Oar. It is a different subject drawn in the same frame and it crowds the left side.
The oar itself is only a gold line skeleton (two tines, one shaft, a short crossbar). It is not a filled silhouette, so the drawing does not read as a solid oar.

Star 6061 (left splash, intended up and left of the left stroke) sits at about (165,192), on the blue figure's shoulder, not in the open space left of the blade. Its droplets would fan into the figure, not away from the oar.
Star 2762 (right splash) sits at about (369,332), out to the right of the shaft and well below the blade. It does not read as spray thrown up from the right stroke.
The wet-hide binding star 4147 at about (283,284) sits at the blade-to-shaft junction. It should sit on the shaft itself, where the wrap ring is.
The T-handle crossbar is tiny, about 29 px wide at y=470, between stars 3909 (about 296,470) and 3455 (about 325,470). It reads as a stub, not a grip.
The labels for 3909 and 3455 overlap at the bottom, and the labels for 4906 and 3786 collide at the top. Two of the labels are also cut off.

Keep the shaft as a single filled band from the junction down to the grip near (296,470). Place wet-hide binding 4147 on that shaft band, about (288,284), as a short ring across it. Widen the T-handle: put 3909 at about (270,470) and 3455 at about (330,470), so the crossbar reads as a grip. Move splash 6061 to open space up and left of the left tine, about (190,95), with droplets fanning up-left away from the blade. Move splash 2762 to open space up and right of the right tine, about (340,95), with droplets fanning up-right. Offset the labels so the top pair and the bottom pair no longer collide.
